answer: The grove multiplier is published, charged in nebula, and sparrow lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 613 identities would post 3079 proofs and burn roughly 54 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
